concept: Responsibility after a concrete mistake: a woman gathers the broken pieces of a mug in her home.

generation.sourceDescription: Original generated triptych; CLEAN is a text-free crop of the left panel. TYPE was separately rasterized with licensed EB Garamond lettering, and THUMB is a separate focal-aware crop.
generation.notes: Original generated imagery, no external photos, logos, celebrities or book covers. Existing accepted source was reused rather than generating a duplicate.

rights.notes: OpenAI-generated original scene. TYPE lettering rasterized using EB Garamond 12 Regular and Italic (SIL Open Font License 1.1); no font binaries distributed. Bible wording is a taxonomy-approved reference only, not a Bible translation excerpt.

accessibility.altText: A woman kneels at home, remorseful as she picks up the broken pieces of a white mug.
accessibility.localeFallback: For tl, ceb, ilo and any unsupported TYPE locale, use CLEAN with semantic localized live text. The English TYPE must not masquerade as translated.

qc.localInspectionNotes: CLEAN and TYPE inspected at native dimensions; TYPE checked at 320x400; THUMB checked at 80x100. Broken mug and reaching hand remain recognizable. 4:5 crop best matches source x≈100/1024 to 920/1024. Typography has high contrast against navy header. No fake text or Bible prose.

repoVisualAudit.warning: Exact audited QA run on another metadata-only Lane Y PR head includes the same published Guilt image and derived binary fingerprints. This is not current production-deployment or independent artwork/context signoff.

browserQA.proof: The exact-run built preview served all 32 manifest-listed image files with matching SHA-256 and validated 8 complete release bundles at 320/390/430 CSS-pixel viewports in Chromium; 84 TYPE/THUMB screenshots across release and draft bundles were captured.
browserQA.excludes: font aesthetic, full editorial/visual artwork approval, independent Scripture contextual signoff, exact deployed production SHA

laneYContextReview.context: The apostle addresses walking in the light, acknowledging sin and confessing sins before God's forgiveness and cleansing; 1 John 1:9 is conditional on confession. The illustrated broken mug is an ordinary tangible mistake and must NOT itself be presented as necessarily moral sin.
laneYContextReview.copyPolicy: No Bible prose in the raster artwork. Future devotionals using this image must distinguish subjective guilt or an accident from moral wrongdoing and must not claim automatic pardon without the verse's confession condition.
laneYContextReview.verified: Reference only; context documented, not final independent doctrinal certification
